US-AR.summary: Act 1060 (Enacted 2025): Clarifies that the owner of AI-generated content is the person providing the input or their employer, not the AI itself.

US-CA.summary: No specific state-level action mentioned in the 2025 report.

US-CO.summary: No specific state-level action mentioned in the 2025 report.

US-ID.summary: I.C. § 5-346 (Enacted 2022): Prohibits the granting of personhood to 'artificial intelligence,' grouping it with nonhuman animals and inanimate objects.

US-KY.summary: H.B. 352 (Failed 2024): Would have revised the definition of 'person' in civil actions to explicitly exclude AI.

US-MO.summary: This bill establishes the "AI Non-Sentience and Responsibility Act" in Missouri, explicitly denying sentience to artificial intelligence.

US-OH.summary: This bill seeks to declare artificial intelligence systems nonsentient and prohibit them from obtaining legal personhood in Ohio.

US-OR.summary: H.B. 2748 (Enacted 2025): Prohibits a 'nonhuman entity' (including AI) from using protected, licensed medical titles such as 'Registered nurse' or 'Nurse practitioner.'

US-TN.summary: This bill defines 'human being,' 'life,' and 'natural person' for statutory construction and explicitly excludes artificial intelligence and machines from these definitions.

US-TX.summary: No specific state-level action mentioned in the 2025 report.

US-UT.summary: H.B. 249 (Enacted 2024): Explicitly prohibits any governmental entity from granting or recognizing legal personhood in 'artificial intelligence.'

US-WA.summary: H.B. 2029 (Failed 2025): Attempted to prohibit governmental entities from granting legal personhood to AI, similar to the Utah/Idaho model.
